deep.reconstruction:
Context: scratch calculus on the verso of a leaf whose other side holds notes on Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' and Laplace. The following page is the gravitation/ether draft. Mathematically the page has no visible link to those texts.

(A) Top two lines, isolated and context unclear. From p u - q z + v = x, with p, q, v treated as constants in u, differentiating gives p - q z_u = x_u, so q z_u = p - x_u. Multiplying by x gives q z_u x = (p - x_u) x. This is then set equal to q(m + n(1-u)^{1/n - 1}), a chosen ansatz. Nothing more is done with it, and I cannot identify the problem it serves.

(B) Main object: the first-order ODE x dx/dy + alpha x + beta = y^mu. This is an Abel equation of the second kind.

(B1) First integral attempt. Put v = ∫x dy, so x = v'. Since x x' = (1/2)(v'^2)', integration gives (1/2) v'^2 + alpha v + beta y = y^{mu+1}/(mu+1). The integration constant is absorbed into v.
- Introduce z by alpha z = y^{mu+1}/(mu+1) - beta y, so z_y = (y^mu - beta)/alpha.
- The integral becomes (1/2)(v_z)^2 (z_y)^2 + alpha v - alpha z = 0.
- Put v = w z. Then v_z = z w' + w and alpha(v - z) = alpha z (w - 1).
- Hence (z w' + w)(w-1)^{-1/2} = f(z). Here f(z) = sqrt(-2 alpha z)/z_y, expressed in z (definition mine).
- Rewritten: c·z d/dz (w-1)^{1/2} + w/(w-1)^{1/2} = f(z). The correct constant is c = 2.

(B2) Right column. The equation dx/dz + 1/x = alpha f(z) is the Abel equation itself in the variable z (my reconstruction).
- Dividing x x_z z_y + alpha x + beta = y^mu = alpha z_y + beta by x z_y gives x_z = alpha/x - alpha/z_y.
- Scale x = sqrt(-alpha) X. This gives X_z + 1/X = alpha·sqrt(-alpha)/(y^mu - beta) = alpha f(z), with f = sqrt(-alpha)/(y^mu - beta).
- Riemann then sets alpha = 0. The reduced equation x' + 1/x = 0 integrates to (1/2)x^2 + z = a, i.e. x = (2(a - z))^{1/2}.
- He varies the constant, a = a(z). Then x' + 1/x = a'/sqrt(2(a - z)), which must equal alpha f(z). Riemann writes a'/(a - z)^{1/2}, dropping a factor sqrt 2.
- This merely trades the equation for another nonlinear ODE for a(z). It is a perturbative / variation-of-constants idea; nothing is concluded.

(B3) Left middle: two solutions and an auxiliary function p.
- He writes two solutions x1, x2 of the same equation.
- He restates alpha v = -(1/2)p^2 - beta y + y^{mu+1}/(mu+1), with p = v_y.
- Differentiating and multiplying by y gives v_y v_yy y + alpha v_y y + beta y = y^{mu+1}.
- He introduces a new function p(y) via the ansatz x = v_y = -alpha·dy/d(log p) ± (1/2) dp/dy = -alpha p/p' ± p'/2. The ± labels the two solutions x1, x2. So their half-sum is -alpha p/p' and their half-difference is p'/2: p encodes the pair of solutions. The note '(1/2)(v1' + v2') = alpha dy/dlog p' has a sign inconsistency; it should be -alpha.
- Then v_yy = -alpha + alpha p (y_p)^2 p_yy ± (1/2) p_yy. This is correct, since d/dy(p/p') = 1 - p p''/p'^2.
- It equals -alpha + y_p p_yy (alpha y_{log p} ± (1/2) p_y), using y_p p_y = 1.
- Substituting into v_y(v_yy + alpha) + beta - y^mu = 0 gives (dy/dp)(d^2p/dy^2)[(alpha dy/dlog p)^2 - (1/4)(dp/dy)^2] - beta + y^mu = 0.
- This is a second-order nonlinear ODE for p, i.e. p'' (alpha^2 p^2/p'^2 - p'^2/4)/p' = beta - y^mu. It is correct.

(B4) Bottom: relation between two solutions.
- Regard x1 as a function of x2. Then x1 (dx1/dx2) x2' + alpha x1 + beta = y^mu and x2 x2' + alpha x2 + beta = y^mu.
- Eliminating x2' = (y^mu - beta - alpha x2)/x2 gives (y^mu - beta)(x1 x1' - x2) = alpha x1 x2 (x1' - 1).
- Subtracting the two equations gives x2' (x1 x1' - x2) = alpha (x2 - x1).
- Both are correct. They are the standard way of seeking a transformation linking two integrals of an Abel equation; no conclusion is drawn on the page.
errors: In z d(w-1)^{1/2}/dz + (w^2/(w-1))^{1/2} = f z, the first term needs a factor 2: (z w' + w)(w-1)^{-1/2} = 2 z d/dz (w-1)^{1/2} + w (w-1)^{-1/2}. The manuscript may have a struck/overwritten '2' there. Also 'f z' should be f(z), not z f(z).
In the variation of constants, dx/dz + 1/x = a'/sqrt(2(a-z)); Riemann writes a'/(a-z)^{1/2}, omitting the factor 1/sqrt 2 (immaterial for the idea).
Sign inconsistency: '(1/2)(dv1/dy + dv2/dy) = alpha dy/dlog p' versus the next line 'dv/dy = -alpha dy/dlog p ± (1/2) dp/dy'; the half-sum should be -alpha dy/dlog p.
The function f(z) in (w'z + w)(w-1)^{-1/2} = f(z) involves sqrt(-2 alpha z), so it is real only for alpha z < 0. This is not addressed (harmless for formal work).
Line (A) has no stated context; the identification of what is held constant in u is my assumption.

results.what: First integral and change of variables for the Abel equation x x' + alpha x + beta = y^mu: v = ∫x dy, (1/2)v'^2 + alpha v + beta y = y^{mu+1}/(mu+1), z = (y^{mu+1}/(mu+1) - beta y)/alpha, v = w z
results.modern_name: Abel differential equation of the second kind; reduction to a normal form by change of independent variable
results.usually_credited_to: N. H. Abel (posthumous, c.1829-1839); Liouville (1886/1903) for systematic reductions and invariants

results.what: Reduction to dx/dz + 1/x = alpha f(z), then the unperturbed solution x = sqrt(2(a-z)) and variation of the constant a
results.modern_name: Abel equation normal form and variation of parameters

results.what: Encoding a pair of solutions by one function p: x = -alpha p/p' ± p'/2, giving the second-order ODE (p''/p')(alpha^2 p^2/p'^2 - p'^2/4) = beta - y^mu
results.modern_name: Symmetric-function (sum/difference) parametrization of two integrals; analogous to Riccati linearization via a logarithmic derivative

results.what: Relations between two integrals x1, x2: (y^mu - beta)(x1 dx1/dx2 - x2) = alpha x1 x2 (dx1/dx2 - 1) and dx2/dy (x1 dx1/dx2 - x2) = alpha (x2 - x1)
results.modern_name: Elimination yielding a relation between solutions (search for a superposition/transformation law)

deep.surprise_reason: Exploratory, inconclusive scratch work on a specific Abel equation of the second kind. The methods are first integral, change of variable, variation of constants, and relations between two solutions, all standard in the 19th century. It is mildly interesting that Riemann worked on this equation at all; the physical source is possibly connected to his natural-philosophy or gas-dynamics work, but this is unsure. No new result is reached.

(z w' + w)(w-1)^{-1/2} = 2 z d/dz (w-1)^{1/2} + w (w-1)^{-1/2}; the factor 2 is needed
